description:
Fetch one URL, or a known list via urls=[...], as markdown; PDFs too; JS pages and anti-bot walls included. Many pages of one site whose URLs you do not have yet: web_crawl.
- A robots.txt-Disallowed URL makes NO request: error='robots_disallowed', content_ok false. Switch source, or ignore_robots=true where you have permission.
- The third tier is archive.org: on a gone/removed page (HTTP 404/410/451 — not on 401/403, which are walls: archive won't hold login-gated content either), content_ok can be true of a dated Wayback snapshot - check source + archived_at. No parameter disables it.
- Touching the page is web_act, and this tool changes nothing it fetches. The deep shape of schema and the browser/session knobs is not here: sys_guide(topic='behavior') is the handbook, sys_guide(topic='call') the placement traps.

urls.description: URLs (parallel; one row each in `results`; check is at most 10)

extraction_type.description: Format: markdown (default), html (raw markup), text, article, structured, or check (changed-since-last-fetch; urls= batch, max 10).

css_selector.description: Narrows extracted content. HTML only - on XML/JSON/plain text the whole document comes back and the summary says so.

max_content_chars.description: Content cap in chars (500-200000; default from DHOLE_DEFAULT_CONTENT_CHARS). The rest stays reachable via offset/next_offset.

timeout.description: Whole-call budget in ms (default 30000; 25000 with actions; max 120000), shared by the HTTP retries; one HTTP attempt caps at 30s (timeout_applied names the figure). On a document URL it is spent on the DOWNLOAD, and a download gets one attempt.

force_fetcher.description: Pin one tier, skipping auto-escalation: 'http' = fast, no JS/bot walls; 'stealthy' = anti-detect browser.

anti_detect.description: Browser stealth level: off, basic (canvas + WebRTC), auto (the tested default, answers Cloudflare), aggressive (auto + every resource). Omit = cred_defaults, else auto.

offset.description: Char offset to resume a truncated page; take it from next_offset.

pages.description: PDF only: '1-5' or '1,3,5-7'. Narrows what is EXTRACTED, not what is downloaded; pick ranges from table_of_contents.

password.description: PDF only: password for an encrypted PDF.

focus.description: Return only blocks matching this query. Applied after the cache, so it does not re-fetch; re-pass the same focus when paginating. Which scorer runs it, and what it costs: focus_engine.

focus_mode.description: Shape of the focus answer: 'filter' (default) keeps every block past the relevance cut; 'best' returns only the highest-scoring block plus its heading. Requires focus.

focus_engine.description: Which scorer runs focus: 'bm25' (default, keyword overlap) or 'neural' (a local cross-encoder, needing the reranker model). Per-page cost: sys_guide(topic='behavior').

schema.description: CSS-driven structured extraction instead of markdown: {properties: {...}} (a JSON string is accepted). Which keys are read, first match vs "type": "array", per-element grouping, the invented-keyword trap and the record ceilings: sys_guide(topic='behavior', section='Structured extraction').

confirm.description: Approval for a sensitive action on this call - today only cdp_url: an attach is refused with cdp_authorization_required unless that host's approval is younger than 30 days, and nothing executes without it. False (default) approves nothing.

session_id.description: Carry cookies across calls under this name (1-64 chars: letters, digits, . _ -). Covers both tiers; values never leave the process.

ignore_robots.description: Skip the robots.txt check for this call (default false = comply). True only where you have the site's permission.

check_login.description: Model-free login probe on the settled browser page; returns login_check (DOM signals + cookie NAMES, never values). Live-only: null on HTTP-tier results and on cache hits.

cdp_url.description: Attach the user's Chrome over CDP: rides that profile's logged-in cookies, skips the HTTP tier and public cache; answers say cdp_attached=true. Attach needs confirm=true per host (30 days).

headers.description: Your keys win, key by key, over what dhole synthesizes. Refused by name, each with its door: cookie / authorization / proxy-authorization -> cred_defaults, user-agent -> the TLS profile, if-* -> extraction_type='check'. anti_detect='off' sends yours alone; caps: sys_guide(topic='behavior').

include_links.description: Also return outgoing links, classified as citations / navigation / external, with a primary_source hint (default false).

max_links.description: Per-list cap for include_links (1-100; default 30/20/20); links.total_found and links.is_truncated report what it hid.

include_media.description: Also return up to 20 image URLs found on the page in .media (default false).

include_headers.description: Also return this response's status line, headers and redirect endpoints in metadata (default false). Set-Cookie comes back as cookie NAMES only; a redirect chain is walked with HEAD, and the call skips the cache because stored headers describe an earlier fetch.

save_to.description: Write this response's BYTES to this file instead of extracting text. Parent must exist; an existing file is refused, never overwritten. Returns one receipt line (metadata.saved_to/bytes/sha256); skips cache and extraction. Pairs with max_save_bytes.

max_save_bytes.description: Ceiling for save_to: default 268435456 (256MB), cap 1073741824 (1GB). Over it nothing is written and the size is reported. The 50MB extraction cap does not apply to a save_to download.

nested_selector.description: Two layers in one call: a CSS selector on THIS page naming the elements to follow; each one's href (its own, a descendant's or an ancestor's <a>) is fetched and nested_fields read there.

nested_fields.description: What to read on each second-layer page: [{'name':'作品','selector':'.work a','type':'array'}] or {'作品':'.work a'}. 1-12 fields; array = every match. Field rules and the carry-over trap: sys_guide(topic='behavior').

nested_max.description: How many of this page's unique links to expand (default 8, max 30). Links the cap hid are truncation=nested_budget; duplicates and href-less matches are counted separately.

name: web_read

description:
Act on one page - click / fill / press / read / scroll / wait / snapshot / submit - then read back what it became. Reading it without touching it is web_read.
- The chain runs in order on the stealthy browser and never from cache; every action leaves a receipt in metadata.actions, and a failed one says what sat at that selector.
- No selector? {"snapshot": true} first: elements come back numbered, later actions address them by index, and expect:'name' verifies the visible name so a stale index fails instead of clicking the wrong thing.
- submit PAUSES without confirm=true (only that step; earlier actions in the chain have run): describe exactly what would go, and on the user's yes re-run the same chain. Captchas: at most 3 attempts, then hand off - each call is a fresh page unless pin=true keeps it. The walls-and-2FA list lives in sys_guide(topic='behavior').
- Credentials never go in an argument: cred_defaults stores them.
- VISUAL ASSIST: {"screenshot": {"selector": "css", "decode_qr": true}} crops one element of the SAME page instance and returns it inline AFTER the chain has run - a step of this chain cannot type what it cannot yet see, so a capture is for a human to read. Text the page holds is what a step CAN answer: {"read": {"selector": "css", "as": "code"}} then {"fill": {"selector": "css", "text": "{=code}"}}. The dict form's options: sys_guide(topic='behavior').
Action-key shapes, index addressing and the lazy-feed discipline: sys_guide(topic='behavior', section='Page interaction').

url.description: The page to act on. One per call - a chain is written against one DOM.

actions.description: ONE action key per object: [{scroll:3},{wait:1000}]. Keys: click,fill,read,press,hover,drag,wait,scroll,wait_selector,snapshot,screenshot,submit,upload,dialog,tab,select,navigate,pdf,evaluate; fill=text,press=key,drag=to,upload=files,dialog=answer,select=option,pdf=save_to,evaluate=expr.

extraction_type.description: How the post-action page is read back (default markdown; also html, text, article, structured).

max_content_chars.description: Max chars of that content (default 40000); the action receipts are never cut by it.

focus.description: After the chain, return only blocks relevant to this query instead of the whole page.

timeout.description: Whole-call budget in ms (default 25000 - sized to beat a typical 30s host MCP timeout; raise it when your host allows more. max 120000).

anti_detect.description: Stealth rungs per web_read.anti_detect; omit = cred_defaults, else auto.

session_id.description: Act inside this named session, so the login it holds is the state the page starts from. Names only, never values.

cdp_url.description: Attach a running Chrome (its own logged-in profile) and act there; an attach needs confirm=true per host (30 days).

confirm.description: A submit reads it INSIDE the action: {"submit": {..., "confirm": true}} - a top-level confirm does NOT release it. Top-level it gates the first CDP attach. Only on the user's explicit yes.

check_login.description: Model-free login probe on the settled browser page; returns login_check (DOM signals + cookie NAMES, never values).

headed.description: Run this chain in a VISIBLE window so the user can watch and step in (log in by hand, one CAPTCHA). Default hidden. A hidden browser already up on that profile is neither taken over nor closed - refused (browser_busy). Consequences: sys_guide(topic='config', section='Variables by scenario').

pin.description: Keep this page for the next call with pin=true on that session: it acts on THIS page, no re-navigation, so the captcha you just read is the one you answer. Needs session_id=.

name: web_act

description:
Send ONE non-GET request (POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE / HEAD) and read back what the server answered. Reading a page is web_read; GET here is refused.
- A write is sent ONCE: not retried (an earlier call may already have committed), not cached, not escalated to the browser, never answered from archive.org.
- A write acts only with confirm=true (the user's explicit yes). HEAD is a probe and needs none.
- Credentials are not a parameter: cred_defaults stores auth / cookies for that host and this call carries them; identity_applied names what it ran on. Bodies cap at 256KB - this retrieves, it does not upload.
- There is no anti_detect here on purpose: a write never renders. Check where a URL goes first: web_read follows redirects and reports the landing URL. Answer shape: sys_guide(topic='behavior', section='web_request').

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL to send this request to. One URL per call - a write is not a batch.

method.description: POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE / HEAD (case-insensitive). GET is refused: web_read owns the cache, the escalation ladder and the archive fallback.

body.description: Request body (cap 256KB). A dict is sent as a form, or as JSON when content_type says json; a string is sent as-is. HEAD takes none.

content_type.description: Content-Type for body, e.g. application/json or application/x-www-form-urlencoded. A dict body defaults to the form encoding unless this says json.

extraction_type.description: How the answer is read back: markdown (default), html, text, article or structured. A server answering a write with JSON still gets that JSON extracted.

timeout.description: Whole-call budget in ms (default 30000, max 120000); one HTTP attempt caps at 30s (see timeout_applied).

confirm.description: Required true for POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE: a write acts only on the user's explicit yes, and stored credentials for the host ride along. HEAD needs none.

headers.description: Headers to send, winning key by key over what dhole synthesizes. The same three families are refused here by name and for the same reason - see web_read.headers.

include_headers.description: Also return this answer's status line and headers in metadata (default false). Best on HEAD probes: Content-Length / Content-Type / cache headers, no body. Set-Cookie returns cookie NAMES only.

session_id.description: Carry and store cookies under this session name (1-64: letters, digits, . _ -): a login POST's Set-Cookie lands in the jar, and the next web_read with the same id rides it. Values never come back.

name: web_request

description:
Many pages from one site (docs, wikis, listings) when the URL list is not in hand; exact URLs are web_read(urls=[...])'s job.
- Caps: max_pages (1-40), max_depth, char budgets, deadline_ms; whichever bites is named.
- robots.txt honoured per page (refused pages error='robots_disallowed', robots_skipped counts them); ignore_robots=true overrides.
- Plans: web_discover's plan_id + resume_token= here fetches it without re-sending URLs. Drop counters and politeness: sys_guide(topic='behavior', section='web_crawl').

url.description: Start URL (crawl stays on this domain)

focus.description: Query: crawl the links relevant to this and focus-filter each page.

search.description: Filter URLs by keyword (URL path + title where a title was read).

sitemap.description: Where the URL map comes from: true | 'auto' (default) | false. A tri-state, so the strings a serialized client sends are accepted too.

max_pages.description: Pages to fetch (1-40, default 10). The first budget a crawl hits.

max_depth.description: Hops from the start URL (0-5, default 2). 0 = the start page only.

concurrency.description: Pages in flight at once (1-5, default 3). Waiting between requests to one host is that host's robots.txt Crawl-delay, not a knob here.

path_include.description: Keep only these path subtrees: '/docs' keeps /docs and everything under it, NOT /docs-old.

path_exclude.description: Drop these path subtrees: '/docs-old' under an include keeps nothing.

max_total_chars.description: Whole-run content cap (1000-200000, default 60000; 0 = no cap). When it bites the crawl stops before the next batch and the summary names the pages left.

cache_ttl.description: Cache seconds per page (default 3600). 0 = force fresh.

force_fetcher.description: Pin one tier for every page, skipping auto-escalation: 'http' fast but no JS/bot walls, 'stealthy' the anti-detect browser.

timeout.description: Per-PAGE budget in ms (default 30000, max 120000); the whole crawl stops at deadline_ms; one HTTP attempt caps at 30s.

deadline_ms.description: Whole-crawl budget ms (default 25000; timeout= per page); soft cap

ignore_robots.description: Skip the robots.txt check for this call (default false = comply). True only where you have the site's permission.

focus_engine.description: Which scorer runs focus here: 'bm25' (default, cheap) or 'neural' (the local reranker model; asking without it is refused, not downgraded).

resume_token.description: Pass back web_discover's plan_id:0 verbatim; next_resume_token continues where the budget bit.

selector.description: With resume_token=: project every planned page to this CSS selector.

schema.description: With resume_token=: JSON-schema projection of every planned page.

name: web_crawl

description:
A site's URL MAP, with no page read for content - one call answers 'what is on this site' before you choose what to read. pages_crawled counts the map's own fetches: 0 for sitemap=true or a held plan, one per step walked. The picks go to web_read(urls=[...]); many pages at once is web_crawl.
- Two prices: sitemap=true reads the site's own index (one request, <lastmod> per row), unset walks links at one request per step up to max_pages; 'auto' tries the index, then walks.
- path_include / path_exclude scope the map ('/docs' is a subtree, not a string prefix); search filters by path + title. A map's SIZE is the site's call: max_total_chars bounds one page of rows and resume_token returns the rows it held back. How to read a map: sys_guide(topic='behavior', section='web_discover').

url.description: Start URL (the map stays on this domain)

sitemap.description: true = the site's index only, 'auto' = index then link walk, unset/false = link walk.

path_include.description: Keep only these path subtrees: '/docs', or '/docs/*'.

search.description: Filter the map by keyword (URL path + title where one was read).

max_total_chars.description: Chars one map page may carry (1000-200000, default 60000; 0 = no cap). A map's row count is set by the site, so this is the knob that sizes a page.

resume_token.description: Pass back plan_id:<rows shipped> verbatim to get the map rows the budget held back - same map, no re-walk, no re-pay.

timeout.description: Whole-call budget in ms (default 25000 - sized to beat a typical 30s host MCP timeout; max 120000, outside 1-120000 refused). On a map this IS the clock: it bounds the call and the single request sitemap=true needs, so a slow index wants this raised, not a retry.

name: web_discover

description:
Keyless search, all 12 default web engines: baidu,bing,bing_global,duckduckgo,yahoo,brave,sogou,so360,shenma,yandex,seznam,marginalia (pool order = reliability tier: stable mains first, rate-limited/obscure last). Returns ranked URLs + relevance, not page content; never answer from snippets only.
- fetch_content=true auto-fetches 3; else web_read high fetch_relevance hits with focus=. A URL you already have: web_read it, don't search.
- sources= adds keyless vertical pools; sort='newest' = stated publish-day order.
- relevance_score 0-1; fetch_relevance high/med/low: fetch high first. engines_consensus counts index FAMILIES (low = maybe degraded pool; see consensus_basis). Engine matrix + source details: sys_guide(topic='behavior', section='web_search').

query.description: Words to search for. Optional only with mode='find_similar'.

url.description: The page to find similar pages of (mode='find_similar').

mode.description: Rerank: 'auto' (default) uses the local reranker when it can; 'neural' demands it (a refusal is named, not disguised); 'find_similar' needs url=.

engines.description: Narrow the pool, max 18 names: the 12 above plus keyed engines that need a key (sys_guide(topic='behavior', section='web_search')).

sources.description: Pools (default ['web']): 'web','news','academic','qa','code','community'. Verticals are keyless; omitting 'web' searches only them and refuses engines=. Their rows never add to engines_consensus.

sort.description: 'relevance' (default) or 'newest': newest orders rows with a stated publish day newest-first; undated rows stay after.

location.description: ISO country code ('US'), optionally with a region suffix ('US-CN'). Anything else is refused rather than guessed at.

region.description: Engine region, passed through as given and folded into the cache key. Omitted, it is derived from location + language.

freshness.description: Time window: 'day', 'week', 'month' or 'year' only; anything else is refused. No engine takes a finer or absolute range.

after.description: 'Newer than' a date: widened to the narrowest engine preset that covers it; date_filter reports what was actually sent.

before.description: Upper bound, applied per row (not sent to engines): provably newer rows are dropped and counted in date_coverage; undated/relative rows stay.

fetch_content.description: Pull the top hits' full text inside this same call (default false) instead of returning snippets.

fetch_schema.description: {properties: {...}} applied to the pages fetched by fetch_content, instead of their markdown - the same shape rules as web_read's schema.

fetch_min_consensus.description: fetch_content only: keep only hits corroborated by >= N independent index families (min 2; 0 = off). Skipped URLs are in consensus_skipped.

min_relevance.description: 0-1 cutoff on the NORMALIZED rerank score. Below it results are dropped, not re-ordered.

min_raw_relevance.description: 0-1 floor on the reranker's RAW score - the one that can call a whole round irrelevant. fetch_hint reports the raw span.

name: web_search

description: One question, one cited evidence pack: searches, reads the top sources, returns each as [n] + URL + its query-relevant text (focus-filtered, not whole pages). Failed sources say why and never fail the pack. For citing, not exhaustive reading - web_read a source (urls= batches) for all of it; more_hits lists the search rows not read.

query.description: The question the evidence must speak to; it is also the focus= filter applied to every page read.

per_source_chars.description: Chars per source after focus (500-20000, default 4000).

timeout.description: Whole-call budget in ms (30000-300000, default 120000), split across the sources.

name: web_research

description: Search pages this machine's dhole ALREADY fetched (the local content cache). No network, no fetch: answers 'which page I read said X' with url + title + snippet + when fetched. Expired rows still recall, labeled is_stale. Pointers, not text - web_read the URL for the page itself. Nothing here knows pages fetched outside dhole.

query.description: Words to recall by (any language; CJK matches by character bigram).

limit.description: Rows to return (1-20, default 8), best first.

name: web_recall

description:
The identity later calls should assume: set it once instead of passing it on every call.
- Seven keys: proxy, profile (the named persistent browser context), cdp (the Chrome endpoint), allow_private, anti_detect (the rung), plus auth and cookies - and those two REQUIRE "host" in the same object. A stored credential with no host would ride along to the next site you read.
- What a call ran on is echoed as identity_applied (names and host scopes only). Values never come back: they leave this process only as request headers to the host they were stored for.
- A bare call reports the store and changes nothing; unset=["proxy"] forgets one key, sys_state(clear=["cred_defaults"]) the whole store. What the caller passes this time always beats what is stored here.

set.description: Keys: proxy, profile, cdp, allow_private, anti_detect, auth, cookies. auth / cookies need a "host" BESIDE them (one name or a list) naming their site.

unset.description: Key names to forget, every host scope of them together. An unknown name is an error, never a silent no-op.

show.description: true = report the store and change nothing. A call with no arguments at all does the same thing.

name: cred_defaults

description:
What dhole keeps on this machine, and how to erase a class of it: the fetch cache, session cookies (keyed by session_id=), engine cooldowns, the stored identity default, the CDP attach approvals, the config knobs, and the reranker's model state (read-only).
- No arguments = the census, erasing nothing: every open session with its hosts and cookie NAMES (a value is a credential - it would land in the transcript), plus cache state.
- clear=["cache"] wipes the content cache; one fresh URL is cache_ttl=0 instead.
- clear=["<session id>"] forgets that session and its browser; clear=["sessions"] needs confirm=true (the loss shows up at your next visit to that site).
- clear=["engine_state"] forgets engine cooldowns + yield history.
- clear=["cdp:host=<name>"] / ["cdp_hosts"] revoke CDP approvals (confirm=true); show=["config"] lists knob NAMES; values via `dhole config list`.
- show=["models"]: which cross-encoder this machine has, whether its files are complete, what THIS process tried. Read-only - dhole erases no model files; sys_guide(topic='fields') for the reading.

show.description: State classes to report without touching them: cache|engine_state|sessions|cred_defaults|cdp_hosts|config|models|all.

clear.description: State classes to erase (config and models are show-only), or one open session id; cdp:host=<name> revokes one CDP approval.

confirm.description: true for an erasure you would not notice as it happened (sessions|cdp_hosts|all).

name: sys_state

description:
Use for LOCAL files the task references (the supported-extension list lives on file_path) -> Markdown, no web fetch. A PDF that has a URL is better served by web_read - it takes the URL directly.
.html/.csv are decoded by charset detection, not assumed UTF-8: metadata.encoding names the charset used (a wrong guess is recoverable: sys_guide(topic='fields')). .pptx/.odt need no extra install; what a text reader cannot carry (layout, images) is named in the output's first line rather than vanishing from it. .json/.yaml are validated, not just echoed. Relative paths: pass cwd when the host doesn't tell the server the working directory.

file_path.description: Absolute or relative path to a local file. Supported: .html/.htm/.xhtml, .docx, .xlsx/.xlsm, .csv/.tsv, .pdf, .md/.markdown/.txt, .json/.yaml/.yml, .pptx, .odt

cwd.description: Base directory for a relative file_path. Ignored for absolute paths.

encoding.description: Charset for .html/.csv (e.g. 'gbk', 'big5', 'shift_jis', 'cp1252'). Leave unset to auto-detect; pass it when the result is mojibake.

offset.description: Character offset to continue a truncated read (default 0). When is_truncated is true, the Next offset this tool prints is what you pass back here - same paging contract as web_read.

pages.description: PDF only: '1-5' or '1,3,5-7'. Narrows what is EXTRACTED, not what is downloaded; pick ranges from table_of_contents.

password.description: PDF only: password for an encrypted PDF.

name: doc_parse

description:
Batch-fetch RSS/Atom feeds newest-first (title/url/published/summary) to track what a source has PUBLISHED - changelogs, release notes, blogs, news. Feeds parse independently, so a dead feed never fails the batch. NOT a general page fetcher - use web_read.
- A site page is accepted: the alternate RSS/Atom link in its own head is followed and the reply says so in discovered_from.
- since= turns it into a poll for what is new; items_older_than_since counts what it dropped.
- An item's summary is a PREVIEW: past 500 chars it is cut and that item says summary_truncated=true. web_read the item url for the whole text.
Reply shape and the unparseable feed: sys_guide(topic='behavior', section='remaining tools').

urls.description: One or more RSS/Atom feed URLs

since.description: Incremental poll: keep entries published at or after this (ISO-8601 '2026-09-20', RFC-822, or relative '3h'/'3d'/'2w') - pass the previous call's newest published value. items_older_than_since counts what it dropped; undated entries are kept, never dropped.

name: feed_read

description: Read dhole's own handbook, one volume per call: how to write a call, what a response field means, how to fix a failure, which knob to configure. The deep syntax of actions, schema and the browser knobs lives HERE rather than in the tool descriptions - read it before guessing at those. An empty or wrong topic answers with the topic list instead of an error.

topic.description: Volumes: start = one-page route map + hard constraints. manual = full SKILL.md. call = writing a call (placement, patterns). fields = reading a response. behavior = deep per-tool behavior. fix = a failure to diagnose. config = a knob. recipes = a multi-step task. Filename is an alias.

section.description: One heading inside the volume, matched case-insensitively (e.g. 'actions', 'PDF', 'engine matrix'). No match answers with the headings that exist.

name: sys_guide
